source_text: Cum vero non diversae generationis diversus tamen appareret status, relucebat prorsus etiam in illo coniugio, cuius reatui suboles sua communicaverat, generationem non fuisse vitiatam.
pass_a_gloss: But when a diverse status nevertheless appeared of not diverse generation, it was altogether shining that even in that marriage, to whose guilt its offspring had communicated, generation had not been vitiated.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: But if the outcomes differed although the mode of generation did not, it would become entirely clear that even in the marriage whose guilt its offspring had shared, generation itself had not been corrupted.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
